'''R2-A5''', also known as '''Ayfive''', was a [[R2-series astromech droid]] with [[Color|green]] and white plating and [[Gender|masculine programming]]. In [[1 BBY]], it spent time causing trouble in the [[spaceport]] of [[Mos Eisley]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]].

==Biography==
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">{{FilmDate|IV|1|[[Luke Skywalker]] being stopped by [[stormtrooper]]s in [[Mos Eisley]]}}</ref> R2-A5 was rolling around the [[spaceport]] of [[Mos Eisley]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] and getting into trouble when the local [[moisture farmer]] [[Luke Skywalker]] was stopped by a group of [[stormtrooper]]s while in his [[X-34 landspeeder]].<ref name="Entertainment Earth" />

==Characteristics==
R2-A5, also known as Ayfive was a [[R2-series astromech droid]] with [[Gender|masculine-programming]],<ref name="Entertainment Earth" /> [[Color|white]] and green plating, and a black [[sensor]].<ref name="Hasbro" /> Like all [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]]s he was manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]]<ref name="IncrediBuilds" /> and stood 93 [[centimeter]]s tall.<ref name="AEYNK" /> R2-A5 was programmed for combat communications was used mainly to acquire targeting data for starfighters and gunnery systems. He was a tough-guy and ready for action at the drop of a [[hat]]. He was equipped with a claw [[Limb|arm]] hidden within his torso and a retractable [[sensor]]scope within his dome.<ref name="Entertainment Earth" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:R2-A5.jpg|thumb|right|R2-A5 originally appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].|250px]]
R2-A5 first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]; however, it was replaced with a CGI [[ronto]] in the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] re-release of the film.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The droid was reintroduced to [[canon]] by a figure pack released as part of the [[Star Wars Pullback Droid|''Star Wars Pullback Droid'']] by [[Tomy]] in [[May]] of [[2016]].<ref name="Pullback Droid">{{WebCite|url=https://www.takaratomy-arts.co.jp/items/item.html?n=Y835469|text=スター・ウォーズ プルバックドロイド Phase２|work=[https://www.takaratomy-arts.co.jp TAKARA TOMY A.R.T.S]|language=Japanese|archivedate=20211130125948}}</ref> In [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], the droid was first named on a card in the "[[Special Edition Limited]]" set of ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]'' released in [[1998]].<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=R2-A5 (Artoo-Ayfive)}}</ref>

R2-A5 appears in the [[LEGO]] [[Star Wars]] 75059 [[Sandcrawler]] set, but is labled as a generic R2 unit.
